paper_metadata.title: Efficient Evaluation of Exponential and Gaussian Functions on a Quantum Computer

summary: This paper presents gate-based quantum algorithms for evaluating exp(-αx′) and exp(-αx′2) using controlled multiplications, with analytical resource estimates rather than hardware runs. The best reported exponential case is 912 Toffoli gates and 134 qubits, while the best Gaussian case is 704 Toffoli gates and 141 qubits; the space-saving exponential variant reduces qubits further to 71 at 1409 Toffoli gates.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum circuit for evaluating the exponential function exp(-αx′) using a refined controlled-multiplication algorithm, with NISQ-oriented gate-saving implementation and resource comparison against Häner et al.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: constants A_i and C initialized from fixed-point binary representations; domain register x initialized in computational basis

problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute f(x′)=exp(-αx′) over a discretized interval

problem_instance.description: Evaluation of exponential function on discretized interval for NISQ-oriented quantum computational chemistry motivation

dataset_specification.description: No dataset; analytic function evaluation with example parameters α=1, x′ interval [0,10] or [0,100]

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical resource estimation and comparison with Häner et al.; Table II reports Toffoli and qubit counts for selected parameter sets
